description: Phase 2 retrieval evaluation set. Relevance labels are line spans read from the real source at the pinned commits, written before any retrieval run. grade 2: the span answers the question; grade 1: useful context. A retrieved chunk hits a span when the file is equal and the line ranges overlap. Unanswerable questions have no spans; the only correct answer is a refusal.

questions.question: Where is the function that reverses a string implemented?
questions.expected_answer: reverse.String converts the string to runes and swaps them from both ends.

questions.question: Where is the Weaviate client initialized?
questions.expected_answer: initWeaviate creates a client for localhost with the port from WVPORT (default 9035) and creates the Document class if missing; main calls it.

questions.question: How does the ragserver query handler answer a question?
questions.expected_answer: Parse the JSON request, embed the query, search Weaviate for similar documents, build a prompt from ragTemplateStr, call the model, render the response as JSON.
questions.why_hard: Three variants of the same server; any one of the three handlers answers the question, so span coverage below 1 is expected.

questions.question: How does the server authenticate users with OAuth tokens?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: there is no authentication code.
questions.why_hard: grep -i oauth over .go and .md finds nothing.

questions.question: What does PrintDefsUses do?
questions.expected_answer: Type-checks the file and prints every identifier in Defs and Uses with its object.

questions.question: Where does the HTTP server start listening?
questions.expected_answer: Each server's main calls http.ListenAndServe: helloserver, outyet, template and the three ragserver variants.
questions.why_hard: Known Phase 1 case: six valid sites; Phase 1 step 6 missed template/main.go and ranked the ragserver README first.

questions.question: How does the outyet server check whether a Go release exists?
questions.expected_answer: NewServer starts poll in a goroutine; poll calls isTagged, which sends an HTTP HEAD to the change URL and reports a 200, sleeping between tries; then it sets yes to true.
questions.why_hard: Known Phase 1 case: Server.poll ranked 6th and isTagged 7th behind a license window and other outyet chunks.

questions.question: How does the hello command decide whether to print the greeting reversed?
questions.expected_answer: main checks the -r flag (reverseFlag); if set it prints reverse.String of the greeting and of the name.

questions.question: What does CheckNilFuncComparison report?
questions.expected_answer: Comparisons of a function (not a function call) against nil with == or !=, for example if x.Method == nil.

questions.question: What is appendUnopenedGroups used for?
questions.expected_answer: It writes the names of groups added by WithGroup but not yet written, one indented line each, increasing the indent level.

questions.question: What does PrintSkeleton print?
questions.expected_answer: A skeleton implementation (method stubs) of an interface type for a named concrete type.

questions.question: Where is the error 'no build information available' returned?
questions.expected_answer: The helloserver version handler returns HTTP 500 with that text when debug.ReadBuildInfo fails.

questions.question: What happens to a line that begins with %toc in the weave tool?
questions.expected_answer: It is replaced with a table of contents linking the top two levels of headers below it.

questions.question: What are the differences between the ragserver variants?
questions.expected_answer: ragserver uses the Google AI SDK and Weaviate client directly; ragserver-langchaingo uses LangChain for Go; ragserver-genkit uses Genkit Go.

questions.question: Why does a slog handler need a mutex when it writes output?
questions.expected_answer: Handlers sharing a writer (for example after WithGroup copies) must share one mutex so concurrent Handle calls do not interleave output.

questions.question: In the third version of the indent handler, how does WithGroup avoid writing the group name right away?
questions.expected_answer: It copies the handler and appends the name to unopenedGroups; the name is written later by appendUnopenedGroups.
questions.why_hard: Four near-identical indent_handler.go files; WithGroup in indenthandler1 and 2 works differently and v4 is a copy of v3.

questions.question: Where does the indent handler reuse byte buffers to reduce allocations?
questions.expected_answer: indenthandler4 keeps a sync.Pool of 1 KB buffers (bufPool); allocBuf takes one and freeBuf returns buffers up to 16 KB.
questions.why_hard: Only indenthandler4 pools buffers; three near-identical copies of Handle do not.

questions.question: How are database migrations applied when the server starts?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: there are no database migrations.
questions.why_hard: grep -i migrat over .go and .md finds nothing.

questions.question: Where is the function that detects the type name of a value?
questions.expected_answer: detect(value) returns the type name; it is also exported as is(value).

questions.question: Where is the check that a string is empty or contains only whitespace?
questions.expected_answer: isEmptyStringOrWhitespace returns isEmptyString(value) || isWhitespaceString(value).

questions.question: How does isAll combine several predicates into one?
questions.expected_answer: With an array of predicates and no values, isAll validates them and returns value => predicateArray.every(p => p(value)); with values it applies that with Array.prototype.every.

questions.question: How does the library connect to a database?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: the library does no I/O.
questions.why_hard: grep -i 'database|sql' over source and readme finds nothing.

questions.question: What does isAbsoluteModule2 do?
questions.expected_answer: Returns a predicate that is true for integers whose absolute value modulo 2 equals the given remainder (0 or 1).

questions.question: Where does the library decide whether a value is a DOM element?
questions.expected_answer: isHtmlElement checks an object with nodeType ELEMENT, a string nodeName, not a plain object, and a list of DOM properties.

questions.question: Where are the individual checks attached to the main is function?
questions.expected_answer: const is = Object.assign(detect, {all: isAll, any: isAny, array: isArray, ...}).

questions.question: How does assertAll build its error message when a value fails?
questions.expected_answer: It picks the expected type from methodTypeMap (or 'predicate returns truthy for all values') and typeErrorMessageMultipleValues joins the unique expected types with 'or' and the received types with 'and' via Intl.ListFormat.

questions.question: How does a negative assertion such as assert.not.string report a failure?
questions.expected_answer: createAssertNot returns a function that throws a TypeError with the custom message or 'Expected value which is not `...`, received value of type `...`' when the predicate matches.

questions.question: How does isPlainObject tell a plain object apart from other objects?
questions.expected_answer: Its prototype must be null, Object.prototype, or have a null prototype, and it must have no Symbol.toStringTag or Symbol.iterator.

questions.question: What can be passed as the range argument of isInRange?
questions.expected_answer: A number (range from 0 to that number) or a two-number array; NaN bounds or anything else throw 'Invalid range'.

questions.question: Where is the error 'Please don't use object wrappers for primitive types' thrown?
questions.expected_answer: In detect, when the value is a boxed String, Boolean or Number object.

questions.question: Which functions throw 'Invalid number of values'?
questions.expected_answer: predicateOnArray, assertAll and assertAny, when no values are given.

questions.question: Why use this package instead of instanceof?
questions.expected_answer: instanceof does not work for all types and not across realms such as iframes, windows, workers or the vm module.

questions.question: What is the difference between the type guards and the type assertions?
questions.expected_answer: Type guards return booleans that narrow types in if statements; assertions throw a TypeError for unexpected types.

questions.question: Which check tells whether a string is a valid URL?
questions.expected_answer: isUrlString returns true when new URL(value) does not throw.
questions.why_hard: isUrlInstance and isUrlSearchParams share the words; only isUrlString checks a string.

questions.question: How does oddInteger decide that a number is odd?
questions.expected_answer: isOddInteger calls isAbsoluteModule2(1): an integer whose absolute value modulo 2 is 1.
questions.why_hard: isEvenInteger is identical except for the remainder, and the helper's name does not mention odd or even.

questions.question: How are the results of earlier type checks cached?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: nothing is cached.
questions.why_hard: grep -i 'cache|memo' over source and readme finds nothing.

questions.question: Where is the HMAC signature computed?
questions.expected_answer: HMACAlgorithm.get_signature calls hmac.new(key, msg=value, digestmod=self.digest_method) and returns mac.digest().

questions.question: Where does the code convert a timestamp into a datetime?
questions.expected_answer: TimestampSigner.timestamp_to_datetime returns datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=timezone.utc).

questions.question: How does TimestampSigner check that a signed value has expired?
questions.expected_answer: unsign decodes the timestamp, computes age = get_timestamp() - ts, and raises SignatureExpired when age > max_age or age < 0.

questions.question: How does the library connect to a Redis server to cache signatures?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: there is no Redis or caching code.
questions.why_hard: grep -i 'redis|memcache' matches only 'Redistribution' in LICENSE.txt.

questions.question: What does want_bytes do?
questions.expected_answer: Encodes a str to bytes with the given encoding and errors; returns bytes unchanged.

questions.question: Where is a signature compared in constant time to avoid timing attacks?
questions.expected_answer: SigningAlgorithm.verify_signature uses hmac.compare_digest(sig, self.get_signature(key, value)).

questions.question: How does the URL-safe serializer decide whether to compress the payload?
questions.expected_answer: dump_payload zlib-compresses the JSON and keeps the compressed form only if it is shorter by more than one byte, then marks it with a leading '.'; load_payload strips the '.' and decompresses.

questions.question: How does the library support rotating secret keys?
questions.expected_answer: secret_key may be a list, oldest to newest; the newest key signs, and verify_signature tries every key from newest to oldest. Serializer.iter_unsigners also builds fallback signers for each key.

questions.question: What does _loads_unsafe_impl return when the signature is invalid?
questions.expected_answer: (False, payload) loaded from the BadSignature's payload, or (False, None) when there is no payload or it cannot be loaded.

questions.question: What values can key_derivation take and what does each one do?
questions.expected_answer: concat: digest(salt + key); django-concat (default): digest(salt + b'signer' + key); hmac: HMAC of the salt keyed with the secret; none: the key unchanged; anything else raises TypeError.

questions.question: Where is the error 'The given separator cannot be used because it may be contained in the signature itself' raised?
questions.expected_answer: Signer.__init__ raises ValueError when sep is in the base64 alphabet.

questions.question: Which code raises 'Could not zlib decompress the payload before decoding the payload'?
questions.expected_answer: URLSafeSerializerMixin.load_payload raises BadPayload when zlib.decompress fails on a payload marked compressed.

questions.question: How do I create a token that carries a user's id and read it back later?
questions.expected_answer: Create URLSafeSerializer('secret key', 'auth'), call dumps({...}) to get a token and loads(token) to get the data back.

questions.question: Why is SHA-1 not loaded until the moment it is used?
questions.expected_answer: FIPS builds may not include SHA-1, so importing it as a default would fail before the developer can configure another digest.

questions.question: When a timed serializer tries several signers, what happens if one finds the signature valid but expired?
questions.expected_answer: TimedSerializer.loads re-raises SignatureExpired immediately and does not try the remaining signers.
questions.why_hard: Serializer.loads (serializer.py 328-343) has the same signer loop but no expiry case; only TimedSerializer.loads stops on SignatureExpired.

questions.question: Which signing algorithm produces an empty signature?
questions.expected_answer: NoneAlgorithm.get_signature returns b''.
questions.why_hard: Four get_signature methods share the words 'signing', 'algorithm' and 'signature'; only NoneAlgorithm returns an empty one.

questions.question: Which command-line tool does the library install for signing files?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: the library has no command-line entry point.
questions.why_hard: No argparse, click or [project.scripts] anywhere in the tree.

questions.question: Where does Click decide how wide the help text should be?
questions.expected_answer: HelpFormatter.__init__ uses FORCED_WIDTH if set, else max(min(terminal columns, max_width 80) - 2, 50).

questions.question: Where does an option look up its value in an automatically named environment variable?
questions.expected_answer: Option.resolve_envvar_value falls back to f'{ctx.auto_envvar_prefix}_{self.name.upper()}' when no explicit envvar has a value.

questions.question: Where is the progress bar line written to the terminal?
questions.expected_answer: ProgressBar.render_progress builds the line with format_progress_line and writes it, clearing the previous line.

questions.question: Where does the test runner replace stdin and stdout so it can capture a command's output?
questions.expected_answer: CliRunner.isolation, a context manager that swaps sys.stdin, sys.stdout and sys.stderr for byte buffers.

questions.question: How does a group find and run the subcommand named on the command line?
questions.expected_answer: Group.invoke takes the remaining args, resolve_command looks up args[0] with get_command (retrying with token_normalize_func, else NoSuchCommand), then makes a sub-context and invokes the subcommand; chain mode repeats this for each subcommand.

questions.question: In what order does a parameter take its value from the command line, environment, default map and default?
questions.expected_answer: Command line first, then the environment variable, then ctx.default_map, then the parameter default; the source is recorded as a ParameterSource.

questions.question: How does tab completion get triggered and produce its output?
questions.expected_answer: main calls _main_shell_completion, which reads the _{PROG}_COMPLETE variable; shell_complete splits it into shell and instruction and prints either the completion script (source) or the completions (complete), then exits.

questions.question: How does prompt keep asking when the input is invalid or the confirmation does not match?
questions.expected_answer: prompt loops: it reads the value, converts it with the type (echoing the error and asking again on failure), and with confirmation_prompt asks again and repeats if the two values differ.

questions.question: What does _make_default_short_help do?
questions.expected_answer: Takes the first paragraph of the help, cuts it at the end of the first sentence, and shortens it to max_length (45) with '...'.

questions.question: What does make_pass_decorator create?
questions.expected_answer: A decorator like pass_obj that passes the innermost context object of a given type, optionally creating it with ensure=True.

questions.question: What is ParameterSource used for?
questions.expected_answer: An enum recording where a parameter's value came from: COMMANDLINE, ENVIRONMENT, DEFAULT, DEFAULT_MAP or PROMPT.

questions.question: Where is the error 'Got unexpected extra argument' raised?
questions.expected_answer: Command.parse_args calls ctx.fail with it when arguments are left over and allow_extra_args is false.

questions.question: Where does Click print 'Aborted!'?
questions.expected_answer: _echo_aborted writes it to stderr; Command.main uses it for Abort, EOFError and KeyboardInterrupt in standalone mode.

questions.question: How is the name of the _{PROG_NAME}_COMPLETE environment variable built?
questions.expected_answer: The program name with '-' and '.' replaced by '_', wrapped as _{name}_COMPLETE and uppercased.

questions.question: Why does Click not auto-correct or expand abbreviated long options?
questions.expected_answer: It is a backwards-compatibility liability: adding a new parameter later could silently change what an abbreviation means.

questions.question: How do I test a Click command without running it in a real terminal?
questions.expected_answer: Use click.testing.CliRunner and runner.invoke(command, args), then check result.exit_code and result.output.

questions.question: What message is shown when a value is not one of the allowed choices?
questions.expected_answer: '{value!r} is not {choice}.' or '{value!r} is not one of {choices}.', built by Choice.get_invalid_choice_message.
questions.why_hard: Other types say '... is not a valid ...', and tests assert the same message text in many places.

questions.question: When a file option is opened for writing, when is the file actually created?
questions.expected_answer: Write modes are lazy by default: File.convert returns a _LazyFile that opens the real file on first use; '-' is never lazy.
questions.why_hard: open_stream, File.convert and the docs on file handling all talk about opening files; only resolve_lazy_flag and _LazyFile explain the delay.

questions.question: How does the progress bar animate when the total length is unknown?
questions.expected_answer: format_bar places one fill character at a position that moves with cos(pos * time_per_iteration) across an empty bar.
questions.why_hard: About 20 ProgressBar methods share the vocabulary; only format_bar has the unknown-length animation.

questions.question: How does Click send usage telemetry?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: there is no telemetry.
questions.why_hard: git grep -i 'telemetry|analytics' finds nothing.

questions.question: How does Click check PyPI for a newer version of itself?
questions.expected_answer: Refusal: there is no update check.
questions.why_hard: git grep -i pypi in src finds nothing.
